claim: E1 is no longer 'never built': the generator exists, the HeLL source is generated and ASSEMBLES at 20,287 bytes, and the budget question is settled in its favour -- the 5+2 xlat2 technique fits with 38,762 bytes to spare, unlike the existing {0,1,2} comparator which has only 1,537 bytes of margin. What remains is control-flow debugging: the image halts with empty output on both engines.
claim_status: ASSEMBLED, NOT_VERIFIED (root cause diagnosed: missing init phase)
design_implemented: two decimal digits read from stdin, separated by any non-digit
each digit classified by decrements over the shared value/value_C1 cells
the 5+2 cycle pair technique is the intended comparison mechanism
output '1' if A < B, '0' otherwise, through the existing OUT/HALT tail

verification.interpretation: not a runner divergence: the program's control flow never reaches the print tail. This is first-draft HeLL that assembles but whose branches need debugging.

budget_finding: The 5+2 technique fits comfortably: 20,287 bytes against the 59,049 limit, 38,762 bytes of headroom.
The existing {0,1,2} comparator (mbir_cmp_lt.hell) has only 1,537 bytes of margin and fails with one new code flag.
So E1's obstacle is NOT the cell budget; it is control-flow correctness. That is the same class of work the repository already recorded as 73 findings for the {0,1,2} comparator.
what_is_demonstrated: The generator, the HeLL source and the assembled image exist.
The technique fits the Classic tape with wide margin.
Both engines agree on the (wrong) result, so there is no engine ambiguity.
what_remains: Control-flow debugging so the comparison reaches the print tail.
A correct comparison over the full digit domain.
Verification over a >=40-vector grid, which this run attempted (100 vectors, 0 PASS).
scope_limits: Only single-digit operands were targeted; multi-digit was not attempted.
The digit reader technique is from the GPL-3 example_adder.hell but no code was copied from it; the source is fresh.

control_flow_diagnosis.method: instrumented trace of c, d, a per instruction (reimplementation of tools/oracle_classic.py's loop) on mbir_cmp_lt_dec.mb with stdin '1 2'
observed: step 1: c=0 executes op 4 (JMP) and jumps to mem[0]=98, so execution lands at c=99
steps 2-26: c=99..123 all decode to op 68 (NOP); the run continues through NOPs without ever reaching IN, the digit classification or the print tail
both engines agree, so this is the program, not the runners
control_flow_diagnosis.root_cause: The generated .hell has NO initialization phase. Every working image in this repository (mbir_m2_loader.hell, mbir_m2_alu.hell, mbir_cmp_lt.hell) begins with a do_init_* chain that sets every data cell to C1/C0 through COUNTER loops, and reaches its ENTRY by falling through from the last init block. My ENTRY is the first code block and nothing initializes value, value_C1, tmp, carry or the N1/N2 cycle pairs, so the U_CRAZY/U_ROT pointer arithmetic starts from garbage and the dispatch never arms.
control_flow_diagnosis.second_issue: the entry JMP at c=0 lands at c=99, which is inside the flag/cycle region rather than at ENTRY, so the wiring of the entry point is also wrong
fix_required: add an init phase: do_init_value / do_init_value_C1 / do_init_tmp / do_init_carry / do_init_n1_high / do_init_n1_low / do_init_n2_high / do_init_n2_low, each R_FLAG_INIT + MOVED <cell>_crazy, chained by COUNTER2_1 exactly as mbir_m2_loader.hell lines 320-380
declare FLAG_INIT and COUNTER2_1 (the loader has them; my source does not)
make the last init block fall through into ENTRY instead of jumping
control_flow_diagnosis.budget_note: the fix costs cells (8 init blocks x ~4 lines plus flag declarations), and the image has 38,762 bytes of headroom, so the budget is not a concern
